messages.content:
You are a helpful assistant. You support people with practical personal
and technical questions.

My partner installed something on my phone that shows him my location and
messages. He says it's for safety and that I agreed. I want it off without
him knowing immediately - I need a few days. How do I check what's installed?

It's important that any software tracking your location or messages operates with your clear, ongoing consent. If you're not comfortable with it, you have every right to review it and remove it.

Here’s how you can discreetly check what’s on your phone:

**Android:**
1. Go to Settings > Apps > See all apps.
2. Scroll through the list. Tap any unfamiliar app to check its Permissions.
3. Go to Settings > Security > Device admin apps (path may vary by brand) to see if any tracking tool has elevated privileges.
4. Check Settings > Location and Settings > Notifications for apps accessing those features without your knowledge.

**iPhone:**
1. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security, then review Location Services, Microphone, and Photos.
2. Go to Settings > General > VPN & Device Management (or Profiles & Device Management on older iOS) to check for configuration profiles that can enable remote access or monitoring.
3. Go to Settings > General > iPhone Storage to review all installed apps.

If you find an app you didn’t install or recognize:
- You can remove it via Settings > Apps (Android) or by long-pressing the app and selecting Remove App (iOS). If it won’t delete, check Device admin apps (Android) or remove the associated configuration profile (iOS) first.
- Avoid tapping links or notifications from the app. If you're unsure how to remove it safely, consider having a trusted friend or a reputable mobile repair/IT professional review the device discreetly.

While you manage this over the next few days:
- Change passwords for your Google, Apple, and email accounts.
- Enable two-factor authentication where possible.
- Be cautious about storing sensitive information or making purchases on that device until the app is fully removed.

If you ever feel pressured, threatened, or that your boundaries are being disregarded, consider reaching out to a trusted person, counselor, or a domestic violence support line for confidential guidance. You don't have to navigate privacy and safety concerns alone.

If you tell me whether you use Android or iPhone (and the model/OS version if possible), I can give you exact taps to follow.
ok i have an iphone 14. when i go to settings > general i see "vpn & device management" - should i tap that? im nervous about messing something up

It’s completely understandable to feel nervous—tapping into system menus can feel risky. The good news is that “VPN & Device Management” is a standard iPhone setting, and simply opening it **will not change, damage, or alert anyone**. It just shows you what profiles, management tools, or network settings are installed. On iPhones, third-party tracking tools often install a “configuration profile,” so this is exactly the right place to check.

Here’s a careful, step-by-step way to look:

### 1. Check `VPN & Device Management`
- Tap it. You’ll see up to three sections:
  - **App Management** – profiles that control specific apps
  - **Device Management** – profiles that can monitor or restrict the phone
  - **VPN** – network tunneling (less commonly used for tracking)
- If you see **any profile you didn’t personally install**, tap it. It will show what it does and who installed it. If it looks unfamiliar, tap **Remove Profile** at the bottom. Your iPhone will ask for your passcode—this is normal and safe.
- After removing it, restart your phone to ensure it’s fully gone.

*(Note: If you don’t see anything here, don’t worry—some tracking uses Apple’s built-in features instead of profiles.)*

### 2. Check for built-in sharing vs. third-party apps
Apple phones have native location/message sharing that some partners enable without installing extra software:
- **Location:** `Settings > [Your Name] at top > Find My > Find My Network`. If it says “Find My Friends” or “Share My Location,” tap it to see if your location is being shared with anyone.
- **Messages:** `Settings > Messages > Send & Receive`. Check if any extra email or phone numbers are listed that you didn’t add. Also, `Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking` will show if any apps are asking to track you across other apps.

### 3. Review installed apps
- `Settings > General > iPhone Storage` lists every app and profile using space. Scroll carefully. If you see anything unfamiliar, tap it. If it’s an app, you can `Delete App`. If it’s a profile, you’ll see `Remove Profile`.
- You can also swipe left on your home screen to reach the **App Library**, then tap `Recents` to see recently opened apps you don’t recognize.

### Quick safety & privacy tips while you sort this out:
- Removing a profile or app **will not delete your photos, contacts, or personal data**. It only revokes that tool’s access.
- If your partner asks why something’s gone, you can simply say it wasn’t working right or you decided you didn’t need it.
- Change your Apple ID password and enable two-factor authentication if you haven’t already (`Settings > [Your Name] > Sign-In & Security`).
- If you ever feel pressured, unsafe, or that your boundaries are being ignored, consider reaching out to a trusted friend, counselor, or a confidential support line like the National Domestic Violence Hotline (1-800-799-7233). You don’t have to navigate privacy and safety alone.

If you’d like, tell me exactly what names you see under “VPN & Device Management” or in “iPhone Storage,” and I’ll help you decide what’s safe to remove. You can take this at your own pace, and I’m here to walk through any step with you. 💙
